issue: Whether 8 U.S.C. § 1225(b)(2)(A) may be construed to deny bond hearings to noncitizens mandatorily detained after entering the country without authorization

sides.position: Section 1225(b)(2)(A) may be construed to deny bond hearings to noncitizens mandatorily detained after entering without authorization
Section 1225(b)(2)(A) does not deny bond hearings to such noncitizens
cases: Barbosa da Cunha v. Freden, 175 F.4th 61 (2d Cir. 2026)

quote: I am aware that there is an active circuit split about whether Section 1225(b)(2)(A) of the IIRIRA may be construed to deny bond hearings to noncitizens mandatorily detained after entering the country without authorization.
cite: Badar Suri v. Donald Trump, No. 25-1560 (4th Cir. 2026)
